reply:
That changes it: TCP is a byte stream, not a message protocol. Multiple sends can arrive in one read, one send can arrive across multiple reads. The server isn't wrong.

Your client needs framing. Add a length prefix (read N bytes for size, then read that many for payload) or a delimiter (read until you hit a marker byte). Without it, you can't tell where one message ends and the next begins—which is exactly what you're seeing.
